POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

WHAT DOES A WORK AT HOME CONTACT CENTER REPRESENTATIVE DO?

This position supports customer service and sales interactions. This role requires you to interact with hundreds of customers each week across the country to resolve support issues, sell new products and services, and ensure best in class customer experience. In addition to being the best in the business when it comes to customer interactions, you will need to be confident, fully engaged, a team player, and dedicated to bringing a positive and enthusiastic outlook to work each day.

Our entry-level Contact Center Representatives are responsible for the following tasks:

  • Listen to customers, understand their needs, and resolve customer issues
  • Utilize systems and technology to complete account management tasks
  • Recognize sales opportunity and apply sales skills to upgrade
  • Explain and position the products and processes with customers
  • Appropriately escalate customer dissatisfaction with managerial team
  • Ensure first call resolution through problems solving and effective call handling

CANDIDATE QUALIFICATIONS

WONDER IF YOU ARE A GOOD FIT?

MCI provides all new employees with world-class training, so all positive, driven, and confident applicants are encouraged to apply. Ideal candidates for this position are highly motivated, energetic, and dedicated.

Qualifications

  • Must be 18 years of age or older
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Excellent organizational, written, and oral communication skills
  • The ability to type swiftly and accurately (20+ words a minute)
  • Basic knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook)
  • Basic understanding of Windows operating system
  • Highly reliable with the ability to maintain regular attendance and punctuality
  • The ability to evaluate, troubleshoot, and follow-up on customer issues
  • An aptitude for conflict resolution, problem solving and negotiation
  • Must be customer service oriented (empathetic, responsive, patient, and conscientious)
  • Ability to multi-task, stay focused and self-manage
  • Strong team orientation and customer focus
  • The ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment where change and ambiguity prevalent
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to build relationships with your team and customers

COMPENSATION DETAILS

WANT AN EMPLOYER THAT VALUES YOUR CONTRIBUTION?

At MCI, we believe that your hard work deserves recognition and reward. Our compensation and benefits packages are designed to be competitive and to grow with you over time. Starting compensation is based on experience, and we offer a variety of benefits and incentives to support and reward our team members.

What You Can Expect from MCI:

We understand the importance of balance and support, which is why we offer a variety of benefits and incentives that go beyond a paycheck. Our team members enjoy:

  • Paid Time Off: Earn PTO and paid holidays to take the time you need.
  • Health Benefits: Full-time employees are eligible for supplemental health coverage through Blue Cross.
  • Life Insurance: Access life insurance options to safeguard your loved ones.
  • Supplemental Insurance: Accident and critical illness insurance
  • Career Growth: With a focus on internal promotions, employees enjoy significant advancement opportunities.
  • Paid Training: Learn new skills while earning a paycheck.
  • Fun, Engaging Work Environment: Enjoy a team-oriented culture that fosters collaboration and engagement.
  • Casual Dress Code: Be comfortable while you work.

Compensation & Benefits that Fit Your Life

MCI takes pride in tailoring our offerings to fit the needs of our diverse team across subsidiaries and locations. While specific benefits and incentives may vary by geography, the core of our commitment remains the same: rewarding effort, providing growth opportunities, and creating an environment where every employee feels valued.

If you’re ready to join a company that recognizes your contributions and supports your growth, MCI is the place for you. Apply today!

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

This job operates in a professional office environment. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will be largely sedentary and will be required to sit/stand for long periods while using a computer and telephone headset. The employee will be regularly required to operate a computer and other office equipment, including a phone, copier, and printer. The employee may occasionally be required to move about the office to accomplish tasks; reach in any direction; raise or lower objects, move objects from place to place, hold onto objects, and move or exert force up to forty (40) pounds.

CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT

All MCI Locations

  • Must be authorized to work in the country where the job is based.

Subject to the program and location of the position

  • Must be willing to submit up to a LEVEL II background and/or security investigation with a fingerprint. Job offers are contingent on background/security investigation results.
  • Must be willing to submit to drug screening. Job offers are contingent on drug screening results. (Does not apply in Canada)

REASONABLE ACCOMMODATION

Consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), it is the policy of MCI and its affiliates to provide reasonable accommodations when requested by a qualified applicant or employee with a disability unless such accommodations would cause undue hardship. The policy regarding requests for reasonable accommodation applies to all aspects of employment. If reasonable accommodations are needed, please contact Human Resources.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

At MCI and its subsidiaries, we embrace differences and believe diversity is a benefit to our employees, our company, our customers, and our community. All aspects of employment at MCI are based solely on a person's merit and qualifications. MCI maintains a work environment free from discrimination, one where employees are treated with dignity and respect. All employees share in the responsibility for fulfilling MCI's commitment to a diverse and equal opportunity work environment.

MCI does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances. MCI will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with local and federal requirements.

MCI will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. We adhere to these principles in all aspects of employment, including recruitment, hiring, training, compensation, promotion, benefits, social and recreational programs, and discipline. In addition, it is the policy of MCI to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified employees who have protected disabilities to the extent required by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances where an employee works.

ABOUT US

MCI helps customers take on their CX and DX challenges differently, creating industry-leading solutions that deliver exceptional experiences and drive optimal performance. MCI assists companies with business process outsourcing, staff augmentation, contact center customer services, and IT Services needs by providing general and specialized hosting, software, staff, and services.

In 2019, Marlowe Companies Inc. (MCI) was named by Inc. Magazine as Iowa’s Fastest Growing Company in the State of Iowa and was named the 452nd Fastest Growing Privately Company in the USA, making the coveted top 500 for the first time. MCI’s subsidiaries had previously made Inc. Magazine's List of Fastest-Growing Companies 15 times, respectively. MCI has ten business process outsourcing service delivery facilities in Georgia, Florida, Texas, New Mexico, California, Kansas, Nova Scotia, South Africa, and the Philippines.

Driving modernization through digitalization, MCI ensures clients do more for less. MCI is the holding company for a diverse lineup of tech-enabled business services operating companies. MCI organically grows, acquires, and operates companies that have synergistic products and services portfolios, including but not limited to Automated Contact Center Solutions (ACCS), customer contact management, IT Services (IT Schedule 70), and Temporary and Administrative Professional Staffing (TAPS Schedule 736), Business Process Management (BPM), Business Process Outsourcing (BPO), Claims Processing, Collections, Customer Experience Provider (CXP), Customer Service, Digital Experience Provider (DXP), Account Receivables Management (ARM), Application Software Development, Managed Services, and Technology Services, to mid-market, Federal & enterprise partners. MCI now employs 10,000+ talented individuals with 150+ diverse North American client partners across the following MCI brands: MCI BPO, MCI BPOaaS, MarketForce, GravisApps, Gravis Marketing, MarchEast, Mass Markets, MCI Federal Services (MFS), OnBrand24, The Sydney Call Center, Valor Intelligent Processing (VIP), BYC Aqua, EastWest BPO, TeleTechnology, and Vinculum.

DISCLAIMER

The purpose of the above job description is to provide potential candidates with a general overview of the role. It's not an all-inclusive list of the duties, responsibilities, skills, and qualifications required for the job. You may be asked by your supervisors or managers to perform other duties. You will be evaluated in part based upon your performance of the tasks listed in this job description.

The employer has the right to revise this job description at any time. This job description is not a contract for employment, and either you or the employer may terminate employment at any time, for any reason.

jobs.description:
About Pragma & FirstLook

Pragma & FirstLook are building the modern operating system for game development, trusted by over 2,000 game studios, including Square Enix, Sony, EA, Krafton, Scopely, Brain Jar Games, and more.

Pragma Engine is the game industry leading backend - cross-platform authentication, social, commerce, player data, matchmaking, telemetry, and more. Works as your backend or with your existing backend.

FirstLook (including creators.gg and player.gg) is the industry leading Player CRM that helps studios and publishers onboard, understand, and retain their players throughout a game's entire lifecycle - from first playtest to live operations. We've onboarded millions of players and power community growth for 2,000+ studios.

You'll be joining a deeply experienced team who have scaled some of the largest games in the world, including League of Legends and Destiny 2. Our team also brings platform experience from Google, Twitch, Amazon, and Microsoft.

We are a Series B company backed by globally renowned technology investors, including Greylock, Insight Partners, and Upfront Ventures.

Location: Remote, based in Europe or North America
Coverage: Strategic accounts across North America and Europe, with APAC support during overlapping hours
Employment: Full time

About the Role

We're looking for a FirstLook Solutions Architect as part of the Customer Success team to work with our largest and most strategic studio and publisher partners across North America and Europe. This is a hybrid role. Half of it is pre-sale: partnering with our sales team on in-depth demos, discovery, proposals, and custom solutions for strategic deals. The other half is post-sale: owning a portfolio of enterprise accounts, making sure they get real value from FirstLook, and growing those relationships through new licenses, add-ons, and campaigns.

Our enterprise customers rarely buy something off the shelf. They run white label playtests, managed creator programs, paid player acquisition campaigns, and custom integrations. You'll be the person who figures out what a studio actually needs, designs a solution that fits, helps close it, and then makes sure it delivers. This is a high-ownership role on a small team, with a direct line to leadership and product.

What You'll Do

Solutions & Strategic Deals

  • Partner with sales on strategic opportunities, leading in-depth demos, technical discovery, and solution design
  • Scope and build proposals for custom solutions, including white label playtests, managed creator programs, player acquisition campaigns, and integrations
  • Translate studio goals into practical plans with clear deliverables, timelines, and success metrics
  • Act as the technical and product expert in deal cycles, answering complex questions and handling objections
  • Ensure a smooth handoff from sale to onboarding so nothing gets lost between the deal and delivery

Customer Success & Account Growth

  • Own relationships with a portfolio of strategic enterprise studios and publishers
  • Lead onboarding, success planning, and regular business reviews tied to measurable outcomes
  • Drive expansion through additional licenses, add-ons, and campaigns, and own renewals for your accounts
  • Identify opportunities to grow within studios and publishers, working with sales to reach new teams and titles
  • Monitor account health and usage, flag risks early, and own the follow-through
  • Bring structured customer feedback and product needs to Product and Engineering

Team & Scale

  • Help shape how we deliver custom solutions as the business grows, turning repeat work into repeatable playbooks
  • Support and backstop teammates on strategic accounts, and help support APAC accounts during overlapping hours
  • Keep account plans, opportunities, and next steps current in our CRM

Requirements

Experience

  • 6+ years in account management, solutions engineering, partnerships, or business development, ideally at a platform or SaaS company serving game studios or publishers
  • Track record of managing large, complex accounts and growing them commercially
  • Experience designing and selling custom or consultative solutions, not just standard packages
  • Experience owning commercial conversations, including proposals, pricing, renewals, and expansion

Skills

  • Strong technical fluency: you can learn a product deeply, understand integrations and data flows, and explain them clearly to technical and non-technical audiences
  • Equally comfortable in a technical deep dive with a studio's engineering team and in a commercial conversation with their head of marketing or publishing
  • Organized and self-directed: you can juggle several strategic accounts and live deals at once without dropping either
  • Excellent written and verbal communication in English

Nice to Have

  • Existing relationships with game studios and publishers in North America or Europe
  • Background in player acquisition, playtesting, creator or influencer programs, community platforms, payments, or e-commerce for games
  • Experience at a games platform or marketplace working directly with publisher partners
  • Additional European or Asian language skills

Location & Logistics

  • Full time, remote, based in Europe or North America
  • Coverage of strategic accounts across North America and Europe, with support for APAC accounts during overlapping hours
  • Willing to work across time zones and travel to industry events and customer sites
  • Competitive compensation, including variable compensation tied to account growth. Benefits vary by country and employment arrangement

Job Summary

Cambridge Investment Group is seeking a Regional Director to provide supervisory compliance, and relationship management support within the Advocacy and Supervision department. This role works under the direction of Advocacy and Supervision leadership to support Financial Professionals by forming strong partnerships with the firm, while ensuring business activities are conducted in accordance with firm policies, procedures, and applicable regulatory requirements. The ideal candidate brings strong judgment, service orientation, and the ability to balance flexibility, accountability, and compliance in a collaborative, high-performing environment.

Key Deliverables and Responsibilities

  • Serve as a trusted resource for Financial Professionals on business strategy, industry changes, branch office growth, and firm resources.
  • Plan regular visits to Financial Professional offices, strengthening partnerships with the firm..
  • Identify Financial Professionals with growth opportunities and partner with internal teams to develop and implement strategies that support their success.
  • Collaborate with Financial Professionals to shape and communicate new policies, procedures, and services.
  • Supervise securities activities by reviewing sales activity, correspondence, regulatory documentation, exception reporting, and related supervisory items.
  • Serve as an escalation contact for OSJ Supervisors and designees, Financial Professionals, and internal partners.
  • Maintain a strong understanding of company revenue and profitability targets, firm-level goals, industry topics, internal programs, departmental procedures, regulatory requirements, and firm policy.
  • Leverage data, reporting tools, and responsible technology adoption to identify needs, support process improvement, and deliver practical solutions.
  • Work in partnership with team members across the firm on strategic projects, initiatives, and service improvements as needed.
  • Interface internally and externally in a professional and courteous manner to support common goals and ensure timely communication of priorities and status updates.

What We Are Looking For

  • Five or more years of related experience, education, and/or training in financial services , relationship management, compliance, or a related field.
  • FINRA Series 7 and 24 licenses are required.
  • FINRA Series 63 or 65, and 51 or 53, licenses are preferred but not required.
  • Strong understanding of supervisory review, regulatory documentation, licensing requirements, correspondence review, exception reporting, and escalation practices.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Adobe Acrobat required; experience with Tableau or similar reporting tools preferred.
  • Ability to adopt technology, use data and reporting tools effectively, and incorporate AI or automation responsibly to improve daily work activities.
  • Ability to travel approximately 8-10 weeks per year for supervisory office visits and related business needs.

Ideal Candidate Profile

  • Builds trusted relationships with Financial Professionals, direct reports, leadership, and cross-functional partners.
  • Exercises sound judgment by assessing information, identifying risk, and making or recommending appropriate decisions independently and collaboratively.
  • Communicates complex issues clearly and explains the reasoning behind decisions in a way that supports understanding and preserves relationships.
  • Demonstrates accountability and ownership in following through on supervisory responsibilities, escalations, deadlines, and process commitments.
  • Brings a service-oriented mindset with a commitment to timely, accurate, and practical support.
  • Adapts well to change and looks for ways to improve processes, increase efficiency, and responsibly leverage technology.
  • Works effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  • Balances flexibility and compliance by exercising decision-making autonomy while maintaining accountability to firm standards and regulatory expectations.

Why Cambridge?

Cambridge has competitive benefits and promotes a work/life balance to encourage individual success. 

  • Premium benefit package including medical, vision, dental, life and long-term disability insurance
  • Vacation/sick time
  • 401K retirement plan with company matching program
  • Eleven paid holidays

You can find more details about our comprehensive benefits package here.


Cambridge Overview:

Cambridge is a financial solutions firm that provides business support services to thousands of independent financial advisors. These advisors offer personalized investment services including wealth management, financial planning, and retirement services to individuals and families across the country. Cambridge provides significant compliance, technology, and transaction processing support to these financial advisors and their offices.

jobs.description:
Overview

HealthEdge® offers AI-powered operational infrastructure for health insurance companies, guaranteeing an enduring financial edge in an increasingly competitive market. We're experiencing strong market momentum, with a growing number of health plans choosing HealthEdge to modernize their operations and compete more effectively. As we expand, we're investing in the people who power that growth, making this a pivotal moment to join us and shape the future of healthcare technology. Learn more at HealthEdge.com.

You Are:

HealthEdge is searching for a highly motivated Utilization Review RN to join our team. As a Utilization Review RN, you will perform prospective, concurrent and retrospective review of inpatient, outpatient, ambulatory and ancillary services to ensure medical necessity, appropriate length of stay, intensity of service and level of care, including appeal requests initiated by providers, facilities and members. May establish care plans and coordinate care through the health care continuum including member outreach assessments.

The Opportunity:

  • Review, research and authorize requests for authorization of elective, direct, ancillary, urgent, emergency, etc. services. Contact appropriate medical and support personnel to identify and recommend alternative treatment, service levels, length of stays, etc. using approved clinical protocols.

This is not a reporting-only seat. We need someone who finds where margin is leaking, quantifies the opportunity, and works with operators to fix it.

You will join an existing, small finance team and report to the Corporate Controller. Expect broad scope, high visibility, and real ownership.

What You'll Do

Gross margin analysis

  • Build and maintain a detailed gross margin model covering cost of service: devices, cellular connectivity, clinical operations, and logistics.
  • Track unit economics per patient and per program, and identify the levers that move margin (device cost, cellular fees, staffing productivity, utilization).
  • Partner with Operations, Clinical, and Supply Chain to turn findings into specific initiatives with owners and measurable targets.

Budgeting, forecasting, and board reporting

  • Support the annual budget and rolling forecasts with driver-based revenue, COGS, and opex models.
  • Prepare monthly management reporting and variance analysis that explains what happened, why, and what we are doing about it.
  • Build KPI packages, scenario analyses, and supporting materials for executive and board meetings.

Customer and contract profitability

  • Build customer- and contract-level P&Ls to show which health system relationships, pricing structures, and contract terms drive or erode margin.
  • Model the financial impact of contract negotiations, addenda, fee changes, and renewals before they are signed.
  • Flag underperforming accounts and recommend pricing or operational responses.

Pricing and APCM/agentification unit economics

  • Model pricing scenarios and the economics of new care models, including Advanced Primary Care Management (APCM) and agentification (automation of clinical and operational workflows).
  • Quantify the margin impact of automation, including cost-to-serve before and after.
  • Support go-to-market and product decisions with clear ROI and payback analysis.

Finance operations partnership

  • Work closely with the Corporate Controller to keep actuals, close processes, and forecasts tightly aligned.

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years of FP&A, corporate finance, or strategic finance experience.
  • Strong financial modeling skills (three-statement and driver-based) and advanced spreadsheet skills in Google Sheets or Excel.
  • Demonstrated experience with gross margin, unit economics, or customer profitability analysis.
  • Ability to communicate findings simply and directly to executives and non-finance partners.
  • Comfort with ambiguity, a bias toward action, and the discipline to get the numbers right.
  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.

Our stack (familiarity preferred): QuickBooks, Salesforce, Databricks, Tableau, Coefficient, and Google Workspace.

Preferred:

  • Experience in healthcare, health tech, or RPM, including familiarity with CPT billing codes, Medicare reimbursement, or value-based care economics.
  • Experience supporting executive or board reporting.
  • Experience in a high-growth or tech-enabled services company with a focus on margin improvement.

What Success Looks Like

  • First 30 days: Learn the business and the data. Map the full cost-of-service structure and current margin by customer and program.
  • First 90 days: Deliver a gross margin bridge and a customer profitability view that leadership uses in decisions. Own the monthly reporting cadence with the Corporate Controller.
  • First 12 months: Own the budget and forecast process alongside the Controller, and have clear fingerprints on measurable margin improvement and on pricing and contract decisions.

Position Summary:

Coterie's GRC team is seeking a GRC Engineer to help build, test, and improve how we manage and validate security, technology, and compliance controls. This hands-on technical role focuses on continuous control monitoring, application and technology control testing, risk evaluation, and the collection and validation of audit evidence directly from source systems.

The ideal candidate combines a strong understanding of risk and controls with the technical ability to work directly with systems and data. You will build and perform control testing, identify control and process gaps, assess associated risk, and recommend practical remediation or compensating controls. You will also support broader GRC initiatives, including risk management, BC/DR, privacy, and other program priorities as needed.

Key Responsibilities:

Control Monitoring & Testing

  • Build and maintain repeatable testing and monitoring processes for security, technology, and application controls.
  • Define how controls will be tested, including testing procedures, evidence requirements, frequency, expected results, and exception criteria.
  • Perform control testing to assess design and operating effectiveness and document testing procedures, results, and conclusions.
  • Identify control failures, process gaps, control drift, and evidence deficiencies, and assess the related risk and compliance impact.
  • Investigate the cause of identified deficiencies and work with control owners to develop practical remediation or compensating controls.
  • Design and implement practical solutions to automate evidence collection, control testing, and continuous monitoring using queries, scripts, APIs, integrations, and GRC tooling where appropriate.

Technical Evidence & Audit Support

  • Retrieve evidence directly from applications and source systems on behalf of control owners for audits, assessments, and control testing.
  • Build and document repeatable procedures for collecting and validating technical evidence, including system reports, configurations, access data, logs, vulnerability results, and change records.
  • Validate the completeness, accuracy, scope, and reliability of system-generated evidence and data used for testing and audits.
  • Support SOC 2, ITGC/SOX readiness, NYDFS, and other audit and compliance activities, including walkthroughs, evidence requests, testing, and auditor follow-up.
  • Maintain organized, audit-ready evidence and testing documentation and retest remediated controls as needed.

Risk & Control Advisory

  • Assess the effectiveness of security and technology controls in mitigating their associated risks.
  • Translate regulatory, audit, and security requirements into practical control requirements and testing procedures.
  • Identify control and process gaps, assess the associated risk, and recommend control improvements, compensating controls, or other risk treatment options.
  • Support technical risk assessments, remediation planning, and other risk management activities.

GRC Program Support

  • Support GRC initiatives across risk management, business continuity and disaster recovery, privacy, third-party risk management, governance, and regulatory compliance.
  • Identify and implement opportunities to use automation, AI, and other technologies to improve GRC processes while maintaining appropriate security, privacy, data handling, and human oversight.
  • Build and document processes, procedures, testing approaches, and supporting materials as GRC programs mature.
  • Partner with business and technical teams on assessments, remediation efforts, and other GRC priorities as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of relevant experience in IT audit, GRC, information security, security assurance, technology risk, or related disciplines.
  • Hands-on experience testing technical security and technology controls and supporting audits or assessments such as SOC 2, SOX/ITGC, ISO 27001, NYDFS, NIST, or similar.
  • Strong understanding of security control domains, including identity and access management, logging and monitoring, vulnerability and endpoint management, cloud security, change management, SDLC, and backup and recovery.
  • Ability to independently retrieve, interpret, and validate technical evidence, including system configurations, access data, logs, vulnerability results, change records, and system-generated reports, including assessing completeness and accuracy.
  • Working knowledge of SQL, KQL, PowerShell, or similar tools for querying, analyzing, and validating system data used in control testing. Software engineering experience is not required.
  • Ability to evaluate control design and operation, understand the underlying risk, identify deficiencies and root causes, and recommend practical remediation or compensating controls.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and professional judgment skills, with the ability to work independently and effectively with technical teams, auditors, control owners, and other stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications (Bonus Experience):

  • Experience with continuous control monitoring, automated evidence collection, APIs, scripting, or integrations.
  • Experience with GRC/IRM platforms such as Optro/AuditBoard, or similar.
  • Experience in insurance, financial services, fintech, or another regulated industry, with familiarity with requirements such as NYDFS 23 NYCRR Part 500, NAIC, PCI DSS, or NIST CSF.
  • CISA, CRISC, CISSP, CISM, Security+, or similar certification.

Our interview process:

Our hiring process generally consists of 4 phases. The goal is to provide an opportunity for us to learn more about our candidates while allowing them to get to know us as well!

  • Phase 1: Qualified candidates will first meet with a member of our People Operations team for a phone interview. This discussion is a high-level conversation to understand more about your background and interests and for us to share more about Coterie and the position.
  • Phase 2: Selected candidates will be invited to meet with our Hiring Manager for a 2nd interview via Teams video. This interview is designed to be more detail oriented and allows you to learn more about the role and expected to be 30 minutes in length.
  • Phase 3: Top candidates will be invited to the next interview round, which will include an experiential exercise project provided in advance, followed by a 1-hour project deep-dive interview with the hiring manager and additional team members, as well as 1:1 interviews with selected team members. jobs.description:

Job Description

Position Summary

In this highly visible leadership role, the Senior Manager, Revenue Accounting and Advisory will serve as a strategic partner to Sales, Legal, Deal Desk, Pricing, Product, Sales Operations, Finance, and Executive Leadership, ensuring the Company's revenue transactions, policies, and reporting practices comply with U.S. GAAP and ASC 606.

This leader will oversee a global team of approximately 7-10 professionals responsible for revenue accounting, deal support, contract review, technical accounting analyses, and revenue policy governance. The role requires a strong combination of technical accounting expertise, operational leadership, business partnership, and analytical capabilities.

The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and possesses deep experience applying ASC 606 within a SaaS business model. This individual must be comfortable leading complex technical accounting assessments, advising senior executives on revenue implications of strategic initiatives, and driving process scalability across a global organization.

In addition, this role will play a critical part in the development of revenue policies, global SSP governance, SEC reporting support, and ongoing enhancement of revenue analytics and reporting.

Responsibilities

  • Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing global Revenue Accounting team of approximately 7-10 professionals, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous development.
  • Serve as the primary revenue recognition advisor to Sales, Legal, Pricing, Deal Desk, and Executive Leadership during customer contract negotiations.
  • Review and approve complex customer arrangements to ensure compliance with ASC 606 and other applicable accounting guidance.
  • Establish scalable contract frameworks and commercial structures that support the Company's growth while maintaining revenue compliance.
  • Partner with Revenue Operations and Finance teams to enhance quote-to-cash processes and strengthen revenue controls.
  • Draft and review technical accounting memoranda supporting revenue conclusions for complex contract structures, new products, non-standard commercial arrangements, acquisitions, and strategic business initiatives.
  • Own and manage the Company's global Standalone Selling Price (SSP) methodology, including periodic analyses, governance, documentation, and executive presentations.
  • Lead the development, implementation, and maintenance of technical revenue recognition policies and position papers, ensuring alignment with evolving accounting guidance and business practices.
  • Drive cross-functional training programs on revenue recognition policies, contracting practices, and commercial deal structures.
  • Collaborate closely with Internal Audit and External Auditors to support quarterly reviews, annual audits, technical accounting assessments, and SOX compliance requirements.
  • Monitor emerging accounting standards, industry practices, regulatory developments, and competitive trends that may impact revenue recognition.
  • Support quarterly and annual SEC reporting processes, including preparation and analysis of revenue-related disclosures and key metrics for Form 10-Q and Form 10-K filings.
  • Develop meaningful revenue reporting, dashboards, KPIs, and trend analyses to support executive decision-making and investor reporting requirements.
  • Provide leadership on special projects involving new product launches, pricing strategies, market expansion initiatives, acquisitions, and organizational transformation efforts.
  • Deliver exceptional partnership and customer service across departments, regions, and executive stakeholders.

Experience & Skills Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related discipline.
  • CPA strongly preferred.
  • 8+ years of combined Big 4 public accounting and industry experience, with significant experience in revenue recognition and technical accounting.
  • Deep expertise in ASC 606 within SaaS, software, subscription, and technology business models.
  • Demonstrated experience leading and developing accounting teams, including direct management responsibilities.
  • Strong experience preparing technical accounting memoranda and position papers for complex revenue transactions.
  • Hands-on experience developing and maintaining SSP methodologies and governance frameworks.
  • Experience drafting accounting policies and implementing revenue-related process improvements.
  • Understanding of SEC reporting requirements, including revenue-related disclosures and MD&A analysis for Forms 10-Q and 10-K.
  • Exceptional analytical and financial reporting skills with the ability to translate complex data into actionable business insights.
  • Experience partnering with executive leadership and presenting technical accounting conclusions to senior stakeholders.
  • Strong project management skills, including planning, prioritization, delegation, risk management, and status reporting.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate technical accounting concepts to both financial and non-financial audiences.

Experience & Skills Desired

  • Primary audit experience serving SaaS or enterprise software companies.
  • Demonstrated success building, mentoring, and retaining high-performing teams.
  • Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and drive alignment across multiple business functions.
  • Strong executive presence and ability to appropriately challenge business decisions while maintaining collaborative partnerships.
  • Proven ability to operate effectively in a dynamic, fast-growing, publicly traded company environment.
  • Exceptional problem-solving and critical thinking skills with sound business judgment.
  • Ability to manage multiple competing priorities while maintaining attention to detail and delivery quality.
  • Strong understanding of subscription-based revenue models, usage-based pricing, professional services arrangements, reseller channels, and emerging technology offerings.
  • Advanced Excel, NetSuite, Salesforce, Power BI skills highly desirable.
  • Experience supporting M&A integration activities and evaluating revenue implications of new business models.

Success Profile

The successful candidate will be viewed not only as the Company's technical revenue expert, but also as a strategic business leader who can scale a global Revenue Accounting & Advisroy organization, develop future leaders, influence executive decision-making, and ensure the integrity of the Company's revenue reporting and compliance framework.

Position Responsibilities and Duties:

Enterprise Risk Management & Strategic Leadership:

  • Lead and continuously enhance the Company's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework.
  • Serve as a strategic advisor to executive leadership and the Board on enterprise, operational, financial, contractual, and emerging risks.
  • Develop and maintain enterprise risk assessments, risk registers, and key risk indicators (KRIs).
  • Establish executive-level risk reporting and dashboards that support informed decision-making.
  • Facilitate enterprise risk reviews and strategic planning discussions across business functions.
  • Identify and evaluate emerging risks impacting construction operations, workforce planning, project delivery, market conditions, cybersecurity, environmental exposures, and regulatory compliance.
  • Participate in major business initiatives, acquisitions, geographic expansion opportunities, and strategic investments to provide risk-based guidance.

Construction Risk & Operational Partnership:

  • Partner closely with Operations and Preconstruction teams to assess risk associated with project pursuits and execution.
  • Support go/no-go decisions through evaluation of project-specific risks, contract structures, delivery methods, labor availability, financial exposure, and owner qualifications.
  • Assist project leadership teams in identifying and managing operational risks throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Develop risk assessment protocols for large, complex, or non-traditional projects.
  • Participate in strategic reviews of major projects and emerging operational exposures.

Insurance Program Leadership:

  • Provide executive oversight of all corporate and project-specific insurance programs, including:
    • General Liability
    • Workers' Compensation
    • Commercial Automobile
    • Umbrella and Excess Liability
    • Builder's Risk
    • Professional Liability
    • Pollution Liability
    • Property Insurance
    • Cyber Liability
    • Executive Liability Coverages
  • Lead annual insurance renewals and long-term insurance strategy development.
  • Negotiate coverage structures, retentions, limits, and pricing with brokers and insurance carriers.
  • Maintain strong relationships with insurers, brokers, and underwriting partners.
  • Evaluate emerging insurance solutions and recommend program enhancements.
  • Benchmark insurance programs against industry peers and best practices.
  • Oversee insurance audits and ensure accurate reporting and premium allocations.
  • Manage project-specific insurance placements and controlled insurance programs (OCIPs/CCIPs) when applicable.

Alternative Risk Financing & Captive Strategy:

  • Lead the evaluation and development of alternative risk financing strategies.
  • Conduct feasibility studies related to captive insurance, self-insurance, large deductible programs, and other risk-retention structures.
  • Develop financial models evaluating Total Cost of Risk (TCOR), reserve requirements, and long-term financial impact.
  • Partner with actuaries, captive managers, legal counsel, auditors, and tax advisors to develop recommendations.
  • Present business cases and strategic recommendations to executive leadership.
  • Oversee implementation and governance of approved alternative risk financing programs.

Surety Program Management:

  • Lead the Company's surety bonding strategy and program management.
  • Maintain and strengthen relationships with surety companies, brokers, and underwriters.
  • Monitor aggregate bonding capacity and ensure alignment with backlog and growth objectives.
  • Coordinate financial and operational reporting for surety partners.
  • Negotiate bond terms, rates, collateral requirements, and program structures.
  • Provide executive leadership with forecasting and analyses regarding surety capacity and future project opportunities.

Claims Management & Loss Reduction:

  • Provide strategic oversight of all workers' compensation, liability, builder's risk, automobile, environmental, and professional liability claims.
  • Establish claims management practices that reduce claim frequency, severity, and overall cost.
  • Manage complex, high-severity, and litigated claims in partnership with legal counsel and third-party administrators.
  • Monitor claim development, reserve adequacy, and litigation strategy.
  • Analyze loss trends and identify opportunities for operational improvements and enhanced loss prevention.
  • Report significant claims activity and risk exposures to executive leadership.

Contract Risk Transfer & Legal Partnership:

  • Oversee review and negotiation of risk-related provisions within:
    • Construction contracts
    • Subcontracts
    • Joint venture agreements
    • Design agreements
    • Professional service agreements
    • Vendor contracts
    • Equipment leases
    • Real estate development agreements
  • Partner with Legal and Operations teams to negotiate indemnification, limitation of liability, insurance, warranty, and dispute resolution provisions.
  • Establish and maintain company-wide contractual risk standards and review processes.
  • Ensure contractual obligations align with insurance coverage and corporate risk tolerance.

Safety, Fleet & Loss Prevention Partnership:

  • Partner with Safety and Fleet leadership to develop enterprise-wide loss reduction strategies.
  • Utilize claims and operational data to identify trends and target high-risk activities.
  • Support initiatives designed to reduce workers' compensation, general liability, and fleet-related losses.
  • Review and monitor key performance indicators, including:
    • Experience Modification Rate (EMR)
    • OSHA metrics
    • Incident rates
    • Vehicle accident trends
    • Near-miss reporting
    • Safety audit results
  • Quantify and communicate the financial impact of safety and risk-control initiatives.
  • Present integrated Risk, Safety, and Fleet performance reports to executive leadership.

Leadership & Team Development:

  • Build and lead a high-performing risk management organization.
  • Mentor and develop team members while establishing a strong succession pipeline.
  • Foster a collaborative culture focused on continuous improvement, innovation, accountability, and business partnership.
  • Champion a proactive risk culture throughout the organization.
  • Serve as the organization's primary resource for risk management education and awareness.

Minimum Skills or Experience Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Risk Management, Insurance, Finance, Business Administration, Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field required.
  • MBA, Master's Degree in Risk Management, or related advanced degree preferred.
  • 15+ years of progressive experience in enterprise risk management, project risk, construction risk, insurance, or operational risk within EPC, industrial construction, energy, infrastructure, or related sectors.
  • Significant experience managing large-scale insurance and risk financing programs.
  • Demonstrated success overseeing surety programs supporting large and complex construction projects.
  • Experience with captive insurance, self-insurance, large deductible programs, or alternative risk financing structures strongly preferred.
  • Proven track record managing complex claims and litigation matters.
  • Experience partnering directly with executive leadership teams and Boards of Directors.
  • Strong understanding of construction operations, project delivery methods, and contractual risk environments.

Preferred Professional Certifications:

  • CPCU (Chartered Property Casualty Underwriter)
  • CRM (Certified Risk Manager)
  • ARM (Associate in Risk Management)
  • CRIS (Construction Risk and Insurance Specialist)
  • ACI (Associate in Captive Insurance)

Key Competencies:

  • Strategic Leadership & Business Acumen
  • Enterprise Risk Management
  • Construction Operations Knowledge
  • Insurance & Alternative Risk Financing Expertise

  • Executive Communication & Board Presentation Skills

jobs.description:
Category: Technology

Location: Jacksonville Florida United States


Senior Tanium Architect / Engineer - Remote
As a senior Tanium Architect / Engineer you are going to support the enterprise implementation and operationalization of the Tanium Autonomous IT Platform on Tanium Cloud, including Tanium Core, Endpoint Management, and Exposure Management.
This is a highly hands-on senior technical role requiring an individual who can provide architectural guidance while actively building, configuring, integrating, and troubleshooting the platform. The ideal candidate has successfully implemented Tanium at enterprise scale across tens of thousands of endpoints and can drive technical decisions, recommend best practices, identify risks, and translate architecture into a stable, scalable production environment.
The engineer will work closely with Tanium professional services and customer security, infrastructure, network, ITSM, endpoint engineering, and automation teams. This individual will serve as a technical leader within the team while remaining deeply involved in implementation.
The goal is to maintain a native, standards-based Tanium environment with minimal unnecessary customization, establish strong automation and operational guardrails, and enable the customer's internal team to become self-sufficient.
Responsibilities
Tanium Architecture & Implementation
  • Lead the hands-on implementation and build-out of Tanium Core, Endpoint Management, and Exposure Management within Tanium Cloud.
  • Translate vendor-provided architectural direction into a scalable enterprise implementation.
  • Review architecture against network segmentation, endpoint populations, bandwidth requirements, security requirements, change processes, and existing tooling.
  • Identify technical gaps, risks, dependencies, and potential conflicts and recommend appropriate solutions.
  • Provide technical leadership and drive architecture and implementation discussions across participating teams.
  • Apply Tanium architecture, agent communication, module dependency, content, and scaling knowledge to implementation decisions.
  • Maintain a native and standardized Tanium architecture wherever possible, avoiding unnecessary customization.
Endpoint Deployment & Management
  • Deploy, configure, and troubleshoot Tanium agents across Windows, Linux, and macOS environments.
  • Support data center, cloud, server, workstation, and end-user endpoint populations.
  • Drive pilot and production deployment waves.
  • Monitor and remediate endpoint coverage, health, connectivity, and performance issues.
  • Support post-deployment stabilization and hypercare activities.
  • Establish automated and scalable agent lifecycle processes.
  • Build dynamic endpoint groups rather than static groups to support scalable targeting and administration.
Tanium Core
  • Configure and maintain sensors, saved questions, packages, actions, computer groups, RBAC, and related platform components.
  • Develop and test custom Tanium content using PowerShell, Python, and/or Bash.
  • Build endpoint inventory, coverage, and operational reporting.
  • Establish role-based access controls and technical guardrails designed to reduce the risk of unintended large-scale endpoint actions.
  • Configure Tanium Connect and other required platform integrations.
Endpoint Management
  • Configure automated operating system and third-party application patching.
  • Establish maintenance windows, deployment rings, endpoint targeting, and approval workflows.
  • Build, package, test, and deploy enterprise software and update workflows.
  • Troubleshoot patching, software deployment, and endpoint-management failures.
  • Configure policy enforcement and endpoint performance functionality as applicable.
  • Support initial inventory and software/license-management use cases, followed by expanded patch-management capabilities.
  • Drive rapid platform adoption, including early agent deployment and patching proof-of-concept activities.
Exposure Management
  • Configure vulnerability and compliance scanning against applicable security benchmarks, including CIS, NIST, STIG, and internal standards.
  • Connect vulnerability findings with remediation workflows.
  • Build security, compliance, operational, and remediation dashboards and reporting.
  • Develop workflows connecting findings to automated remediation where appropriate.
ServiceNow Integration
  • Design, implement, and validate robust Tanium and ServiceNow integrations.
  • Integrate Tanium endpoint and asset information with the ServiceNow CMDB.
  • Support CMDB-driven and two-way integration patterns between Tanium and ServiceNow.
  • Enable CI and tag lifecycle changes to drive appropriate endpoint actions.
  • Align business application, service, environment, ownership, and related endpoint tagging with ServiceNow data.
  • Connect patching and software-deployment activities with ServiceNow change-management processes.
  • Route vulnerability and incident information into appropriate ServiceNow workflows.
  • Monitor and troubleshoot data synchronization and integration issues.
Automation & API Integration
  • Develop integrations using Tanium APIs and automation frameworks.
  • Use Ansible for Tanium agent deployment and lifecycle management across Linux and server environments.
  • Develop Ansible playbooks and automation that complement Tanium-driven remediation.
  • Define appropriate functional boundaries between Tanium and existing configuration-management and automation platforms to minimize duplication and conflicts.
  • Document integration architecture, data flows, automation logic, and troubleshooting procedures.
Dashboards & Reporting
  • Build actionable dashboards for endpoint operations, security, compliance, inventory, and management stakeholders.
  • Support One Insights use cases and dashboard configuration.
  • Develop appropriate dashboard segmentation for workstation and server populations and their respective ownership groups.
  • Establish reporting for platform health, endpoint coverage, software inventory, vulnerabilities, compliance, and remediation.
Collaboration & Knowledge Transfer
  • Work directly with Tanium professional services and customer security, infrastructure, networking, ITSM, endpoint, and automation teams.
  • Serve as a senior technical resource who can drive architecture and implementation discussions.
  • Participate in change-management, rollout planning, testing, and production-readiness activities.
  • Produce technical runbooks, test plans, architecture documentation, troubleshooting guides, and as-built documentation.
  • Train customer administrators and operators on the implementation and ongoing platform management.
  • Drive knowledge transfer with the objective of enabling the internal team to operate the Tanium environment independently.
Required Qualifications
  • 5+ years of experience in endpoint management, infrastructure engineering, or security engineering.
  • 2-5+ years of hands-on Tanium experience within large enterprise environments.
  • Demonstrated experience implementing and operating Tanium across tens of thousands of endpoints.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Tanium Core and multiple Tanium capabilities such as Patch, Deploy, Comply, Endpoint Management, and Exposure Management.
  • Strong working knowledge of Tanium Cloud and enterprise Tanium architecture.
  • Demonstrated ability to function as both aTanium architect and hands-on engineer.
  • Strong experience integratingTanium with ServiceNow, including CMDB-driven integrations and data synchronization.
  • Hands-on experience with ServiceNow CMDB and Change Management.
  • Strong Ansible experience, including playbooks, roles, automation, and inventory management.
  • Experience building API-based integrations and automated workflows.
  • Strong scripting skills using PowerShell and Python and/or Bash.
  • Experience building Tanium sensors, packages, actions, targeting, and custom content.
  • Strong Windows and Linux systems administration experience.
  • Working knowledge of Active Directory and enterprise networking concepts.
  • Experience designing dynamic endpoint groups, RBAC, and operational guardrails.
  • Experience with enterprise software inventory and software/license management.
  • Knowledge of vulnerability management and security/compliance frameworks such as CIS, NIST, and STIG.
  • Ability to independently troubleshoot complex implementation and production issues.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including technical documentation and knowledge transfer.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Tanium certifications such as Tanium Certified Operator or Administrator.
  • Extensive hands-on experience with Tanium Cloud.
  • Experience with One Insights and enterprise Tanium dashboarding.
  • Advanced Tanium and ServiceNow integration experience, including CMDB synchronization and vulnerability-management workflows.
  • Experience with Ansible Automation Platform.
  • ServiceNow or Red Hat certifications such as CSA or RHCE.
  • Experience migrating from SCCM/MECM, BigFix, or similar endpoint-management platforms.
  • Experience working within highly regulated enterprise environments.
  • Previous experience working alongside vendor professional services teams.
Tools and Technologies
  • Tanium Cloud
  • Tanium Core
  • Tanium Endpoint Management
  • Tanium Exposure Management
  • Tanium Patch / Deploy / Comply
  • Tanium Connect
  • One Insights
  • ServiceNow / CMDB / Change Management

  • PowerShell
  • Python
  • Bash
  • REST APIs / Automation
  • Windows
  • Linux

  • CIS / NIST / STIG frameworks

Job Title: Domain Researcher, Finance (M&A)

The Role

Join our research team as a Domain Researcher (DR), where you'll help advance AI-powered financial reasoning, with a focus on Corporate Development, Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A), and strategic transactions.

We're looking for professionals with hands-on experience in corporate development, acquisition evaluation, and M&A execution who can translate real-world financial expertise into rigorous AI evaluation frameworks.

What You'll Be Doing

  1. Design and develop evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, and scoring methodologies for AI agents operating in corporate development and M&A workflows.
  2. Create realistic test cases covering acquisition screening, valuation, financial due diligence, deal structuring, and strategic investment decisions.
  3. Evaluate AI-generated financial analyses, valuation models, acquisition assessments, and investment recommendations.
  4. Translate real-world M&A experience into structured datasets, research scenarios, and measurable evaluation criteria.
  5. Collaborate with AI researchers, engineers, and product teams to identify model limitations and improve financial reasoning capabilities.
  6. Conduct applied research and document findings to advance AI performance in corporate finance and acquisition-related tasks.

What We're Looking For

  1. Strong professional experience in Corporate Development, M&A, Investment Banking, Private Equity, or Strategic Investments, with direct exposure to acquisition-related transactions.
  2. Hands-on experience across the M&A lifecycle, including target screening, valuation, due diligence, transaction analysis, or deal execution.
  3. Strong understanding of acquisition strategies, financial modeling, company valuation (DCF, comparables, precedent transactions), and strategic fit assessments.
  4. Experience preparing or evaluating investment memoranda, acquisition recommendations, and transaction-related financial analyses.
  5. Ability to translate complex financial workflows into structured research questions, evaluation frameworks, and measurable criteria.
  6. Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across technical and non-technical teams.
  7. Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Accounting, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Direct experience within an in-house Corporate Development team, particularly involving buy-side acquisitions.
  2. Experience executing or supporting M&A transactions from target identification through due diligence and closing.
  3. Background in technology-sector acquisitions, SaaS businesses, or strategic investments.
  4. MBA, CFA, or relevant advanced financial qualifications.
  5. Familiarity with AI agents, large language models, AI evaluation methodologies, or financial AI applications.

About Us

Scorpion is the leading provider of technology and services helping local businesses thrive. We do this by helping customers understand local market dynamics, make the most of their marketing, and deliver experiences their customers will love. We offer tools to know what’s going on with marketing, competitors, and customers. We offer a unique blend of AI support and teams of real human people with local expertise committed to customer success. At Scorpion, we are ready to do whatever it takes to help our clients reach their goals. Our technology and personalized tools bring everything together to help local businesses easily understand their unique business, market, and customer needs. We put SEO, Reviews, Advertising, Email Marketing, Chat and Messaging, Social Media, Website, Lead Management, Appointment Scheduling, and more to work for local businesses. We’re a technology-led service with a human touch.

About the Role

Scorpion is looking for a Sales Account Executive to drive new business growth within the legal industry through our AI-powered marketing and technology platform. This is a true hunter role where you'll build your own pipeline, develop relationships with law firm owners and decision-makers, and own the sales process from prospecting through close.

We're looking for someone who understands the challenges law firms face and can confidently have strategic conversations about lead generation, marketing ROI, client acquisition, and revenue growth.

Whether you've sold software, legal technology, CRM, marketing services, case management solutions, or other business solutions to law firms, your industry expertise is what matters most.

If you're energized by opening new doors, winning new clients, and helping law firms grow, we'd love to meet you.

What Your Success Will Look Like

  • Own the Full Sales Cycle: Generate and close new business by owning the sales process from prospecting through discovery, demonstration, proposal, negotiation, and close.
  • Build Your Own Pipeline: Develop new opportunities through outbound prospecting, networking, referrals, and strategic business development. Success in this role comes from consistently creating your own pipeline.
  • Sell to Law Firm Decision-Makers: Build trusted relationships with law firm owners, partners, administrators, and executive decision-makers by understanding their goals and presenting solutions that drive measurable business growth.
  • Leverage Your Industry Expertise: Use your knowledge of the legal industry to identify business challenges and recommend AI-powered marketing and technology solutions that help law firms generate higher-quality leads, improve conversion rates, maximize marketing ROI, and grow revenue.
  • Become a Product Expert: Develop expertise in Scorpion's RevenueMAX platform, including AI-powered advertising, lead management, websites, SEO, reputation management, revenue intelligence, and client engagement solutions. Conduct discovery calls, customize demonstrations, and recommend solutions that align with each firm's business goals.
  • Deliver Results: Consistently achieve and exceed monthly recurring revenue goals through a consultative, solution-based sales approach while maintaining an accurate forecast and healthy pipeline.
  • Continuously Improve: Seek coaching, embrace feedback, and stay current on legal industry trends, AI, and digital marketing innovations to continuously improve your sales performance.

Who You Are and What You Bring

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Sales, Marketing, Communications, or a related field—or equivalent practical experience.

Experience

  • 4+ years of full-cycle B2B sales experience in a quota-carrying role with responsibility for prospecting, discovery, demonstrations, negotiation, and closing new business.
  • 2+ years of experience selling software, technology, marketing, legal technology, CRM, case management solutions, or other business solutions directly to law firms or businesses within the legal industry. You understand the challenges law firms face and can speak their language.
  • Proven success meeting or exceeding sales quotas while independently developing and closing new client relationships. Experience earning promotions, sales recognition, or President's Club is a plus.

Skills

  • Hunter Mentality: You thrive on prospecting, opening new doors, and winning new business. You're energized by building your own pipeline and owning the full sales cycle from prospecting through close.
  • Consultative Selling: You uncover business challenges, ask thoughtful questions, and position solutions that help customers generate measurable business growth and maximize their return on investment.
  • Technology Proficiency: Experience using Salesforce or another CRM, along with modern sales tools, to manage pipeline, forecast accurately, and drive sales productivity.
  • Collaborative Spirit: You enjoy working cross-functionally with teammates and contribute to a high-performing, team-first culture while remaining accountable for your individual results.
  • Growth Mindset: You seek coaching, embrace feedback, and continuously improve your sales skills, industry knowledge, and business acumen.

Your First 90 Days

  • Learn the Scorpion Way: Complete Scorpion's immersive three-week onboarding program with our Client Experience & Enablement team. You'll develop expertise in our AI-powered marketing platform, consultative sales methodology, and the legal industry while learning from experienced sales leaders and peers.
  • Build Momentum: Begin prospecting, building your pipeline, conducting discovery meetings, and delivering tailored demonstrations with ongoing coaching and support from your manager and enablement team.
  • Ramp to Success: Build the confidence, product knowledge, and sales skills needed to achieve full quota within your first three months while continuing to receive coaching and professional development.

Our Scorpion Values

Winning Mindset: When our clients win, we win.
Genuine Care: We only succeed when we are truly invested in our clients and each other.
Unmatched Results: We deliver more than expected–and then some–driving the best results and impacting lives.
Constant Improvement: We believe there is always a better way. We learn we ask “What if?” we build and then do it again.
Unbeatable Teamwork: We come from different backgrounds but have the same vision. We only get there by doing it together, as a team.

Compensation

We acknowledge that states have passed legislation promoting pay transparency. As a national employer, Scorpion has made the decision to post our expected pay rate or pay range (as applicable) in all our job postings, regardless of geographic location.

  • The base salary is $60,000 (entry-level) - $79,000 (highly experienced). This position's base salary + annual variable is $128,000 (entry-level) - $147,000 (highly experienced), exclusive of fringe benefits. If you are hired at Scorpion, your final base salary compensation will be determined based on factors such as geographic location, skills, education, and/or experience. Additionally, we believe in the importance of pay equity and consider the internal equity of our current team members as a part of any final offer. Please keep in mind that the range mentioned above is the total salary + annual variable range for the role. Hiring at the maximum of the range would not be typical in order to allow for future & continued salary growth.

Our Benefits

We invest in our employees by offering them diverse benefits from best-in-class carriers. These benefits provide enough choice and flexibility to keep our employees and their families healthy and happy—today and tomorrow.

  • 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Flexible paid time off, so you can rest, relax, and recharge away from work

Work Location & Flexibility

jobs.excerpt: CyberSheath Services International LLC is a rapidly growing Managed Services Provider primarily focused on providing Cybersecurity services to the Defense Industrial Base (DIB).
jobs.description:
CyberSheath Services International LLC is a rapidly growing Managed Services Provider primarily focused on providing Cybersecurity services to the Defense Industrial Base (DIB). We are excited to be expanding our staff due to our growth and are looking to add a Marketing Generalist to our team! 

CyberSheath integrates compliance and threat mitigation efforts and eliminates redundant security practices that don’t improve and, in fact, may weaken an organization’s security posture. Our professionals tell clients where to stop spending, where to invest, and how to take what they are already doing and integrate it in a way that delivers improved security.  

Successful candidates for CyberSheath are self-motivated, think out of the box, work, and solve issues independently. Additionally, our most successful people are self-starters and willing to put on many hats in order to succeed. CyberSheath is fast-growing and seeks candidates who want to be part of our upward trajectory. 

Position Overview

The Demand Generation Manager will own the strategy, execution, measurement, and optimization of multichannel demand-generation programs. This role will be responsible for converting CyberSheath’s market expertise into awareness, engagement, qualified demand, sales opportunities, and measurable pipeline contribution.

The ideal candidate combines B2B demand-generation expertise with strong campaign operations, content instincts, analytical rigor, and the ability to collaborate closely with Sales, subject-matter experts, external partners, and marketing leadership. They are equally comfortable developing a quarterly campaign plan, writing campaign briefs, launching a webinar nurture sequence, analyzing funnel performance, and recommending changes based on data.

Key Responsibilities

Demand Generation Strategy

  • Develop and execute a scalable, full-funnel demand-generation strategy aligned to CyberSheath’s revenue objectives, ideal customer profile, priority verticals, buyer personas, and sales motions.
  • Build integrated campaign plans that create awareness, capture demand, nurture prospects, accelerate opportunities, and support expansion or cross-sell opportunities.
  • Define targeted campaigns for key audiences, including DIB owners and executives, CISOs, CIOs, IT directors, compliance leaders, security practitioners, contracts leaders, and operations stakeholders.
  • Translate complex compliance and security topics into clear, buyer-centered messaging that emphasizes business outcomes, risk reduction, contract readiness, operational continuity, and long-term compliance readiness.
  • Establish campaign themes and content pillars around CMMC 2.0, NIST SP 800-171, DFARS, CUI protection, compliance gaps, assessments, remediation, managed services, and secure federal enclave offerings.
  • Partner with executive leadership and subject-matter experts to identify timely market opportunities, regulatory developments, customer pain points, and thought-leadership angles.

Campaign Development and Execution

  • Plan, launch, manage, and optimize integrated campaigns across email, paid media, organic social, webinars, virtual events, field events, partner marketing, landing pages, content syndication, retargeting, and other relevant channels.
  • Build campaign journeys for prospects at different stages of maturity, from early awareness of CMMC requirements through active evaluation of compliance solutions.
  • Develop campaign briefs that define target audience, objective, message, offer, channels, assets, timeline, budget, success metrics, and follow-up requirements.
  • Coordinate the creation of campaign assets, including landing pages, email sequences, advertisements, webinar materials, reports, checklists, guides, case studies, customer stories, and sales enablement materials.
  • Manage campaign calendars and ensure programs launch on time, meet quality standards, and align with broader company priorities.
  • Run A/B tests across audiences, messaging, subject lines, offers, landing pages, calls to action, creative, and channels to improve conversion and efficiency.
  • Support event and webinar demand generation before, during, and after programs, including registration strategy, promotional plans, attendance conversion, follow-up nurture, and opportunity acceleration.

Lead Management and Lifecycle Marketing

  • Partner with Sales leadership to define and maintain lead-management processes, including lead stages, lead scoring, routing, qualification criteria, service-level expectations, and feedback loops.
  • Build and optimize nurture programs that educate prospects, establish CyberSheath’s credibility, and move accounts toward sales engagement.
  • Segment audiences based on company profile, role, compliance maturity, engagement history, intent signals, customer lifecycle stage, and buyer behavior.
  • Ensure leads are routed accurately and promptly, and work with Sales to improve conversion from marketing-qualified lead through opportunity and closed revenue.
  • Develop targeted account-based marketing programs for strategic accounts, named-account lists, high-value verticals, and partner-led opportunities.
  • Help Sales teams engage buying committees with coordinated messaging and content tailored to business, technical, and compliance concerns.

Performance Measurement and Optimization

  • Own campaign reporting and provide clear, actionable insights on performance, including engagement, conversion, qualified leads, meetings, opportunities, pipeline, revenue influence, cost per lead, cost per opportunity, and return on marketing investment.
  • Monitor funnel health and identify friction points from first touch through opportunity creation and closed-won revenue.
  • Create regular performance reviews for marketing and revenue leadership, translating results into recommendations, priorities, and next actions.
  • Maintain disciplined campaign attribution and tracking practices in collaboration with Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, and Marketing Operations.
  • Use data to reallocate budget, improve underperforming programs, prioritize high-converting channels, and inform future campaign strategy.
  • Establish benchmarks and operational standards for campaign performance, audience engagement, lead quality, and pipeline contribution.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with Sales to ensure campaigns support active pipeline goals, account priorities, field needs, and market feedback.
  • Partner with product, service delivery, customer success, and cybersecurity subject-matter experts to create technically accurate, commercially relevant programs.
  • Collaborate with content, creative, digital, operations, and external agency partners to deliver high-quality work efficiently.
  • Equip sales teams with campaign context, prospect insights, follow-up guidance, relevant content, and messaging that improves conversion.
  • Participate in regular revenue meetings to share campaign performance, market signals, lead-quality insights, and recommended actions.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, communications, or a related discipline; equivalent relevant experience will also be considered.
  • 5+ years of progressive B2B demand generation, growth marketing, field marketing, lifecycle marketing, or integrated campaign experience.
  • Demonstrated success building multichannel campaigns that produced measurable pipeline and revenue impact—not simply lead volume.
  • Experience marketing complex B2B technology, professional services, cybersecurity, compliance, cloud, IT infrastructure, or regulated-industry solutions.
  • Strong knowledge of demand-generation fundamentals, including audience segmentation, buyer journeys, campaign orchestration, lead scoring, nurture strategy, conversion optimization, and attribution.
  • Experience using CRM and marketing-automation platforms, such as Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Pardot/Account Engagement, or comparable systems.
  • Proficiency with marketing analytics, campaign reporting, spreadsheet analysis, and dashboarding tools.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to simplify technical concepts without sacrificing credibility.
